answer: Each identity claims one harbor berth and locks 70 credits in the reef ledger, which lists berths. Berths are priced in bands of ten: the nadir levy floor is 5, and band b pays 5 plus 10 times b squared, so the 1000th berth in band 99 pays 98015. Auditors recompute the levy from the count; a mismatch burns the bond. One thousand fakes lock 70000 and pay 32840000, unpoolable because each levy binds one key to one berth. A rented-berth ring fails when a reused certificate is rejected and burns bonds. An honest agent claims one berth, pays 5 once, and recovers the bond after one epoch.
